assessment_summary:
Proof attempt:
1. Let G be a finite simple undirected graph with chromatic number k = chi(G).
2. Let v_1, v_2, ..., v_n be an arbitrary ordering of the vertices of G.
3. By definition of chromatic number, the vertices of G can be partitioned into k independent sets I_1, I_2, ..., I_k.
4. When processing a vertex v_i in the greedy coloring algorithm, v_i belongs to exactly one independent set I_j.
5. Since I_j is an independent set, v_i has no neighbors in I_j.
6. Therefore, all neighbors of v_i must belong to the other k-1 independent sets.
7. Consequently, the previously colored neighbors of v_i can have at most k-1 different colors assigned by the greedy algorithm.
8. Because at most k-1 colors appear on the previously colored neighbors of v_i, there is at least one color in the set {1, 2, ..., k} that is not used by any neighbor.
9. Thus, the smallest available positive integer for v_i is at most k.
10. As this holds for all vertices v_i, the greedy coloring uses at most k = chi(G) colors.
11. Since chi(G) <= chi(G) + 1, the greedy coloring uses at most chi(G) + 1 colors on every graph for any vertex ordering.

Evaluations:
1. Justified. Valid setup introducing the graph and its chromatic number.
2. Justified. Valid setup for the greedy coloring algorithm.
3. Justified. Valid consequence of chi(G) = k.
4. Justified. Valid, as the independent sets partition the vertices.
5. Justified. Valid, by definition of an independent set.
6. Justified. Valid, follows directly from Steps 4 and 5.
7. UNJUSTIFIED. Two neighbors of v_i in the same independent set I_m might be assigned different colors by the greedy algorithm, exceeding k-1 colors.
8. UNJUSTIFIED. Relies on the false upper bound established in Step 7.
9. UNJUSTIFIED. Relies on the flawed conclusion of Step 8.
10. UNJUSTIFIED. Relies on Step 9.
11. UNJUSTIFIED. Relies on the false conclusion of Step 10.
counterexample: The crown graph (K_{4,4} minus a perfect matching, chi=2) with vertices A={a1,a2,a3,a4}, B={b1,b2,b3,b4} and ordering a1, b1, a2, b2, a3, b3, a4, b4 uses 4 colors, which is > chi(G)+1=3.
